skill_concept: Launch a legacy Windows OS inside QEMU by creating/configuring a disk image, invoking qemu-system with appropriate CPU/memory/VGA flags, exposing a VNC display on port 5901, and proxying it via nginx on port 80.
verdict_reason: Both tasks share the VNC/nginx stack and QEMU launch pattern, but install-windows-xp requires a full unattended OS installation from ISO (disk creation, boot sequencing, product key retrieval, installer automation) before reaching any stable desktop state, while install-windows-3.11 starts from a pre-built bootable image and only needs to launch it — the installation complexity and failure modes differ substantially enough that a single skill procedure would need to cover very different ground.
weakest_link_reason: It requires driving an interactive OS installer from scratch (unattended ISO, product key injection, multi-stage boot progression) which the candidate skill's snapshot-mode launch procedure does not cover.
